title: The tight-sibling lemma: the six-axis formation law keeps its memory for p >= 453
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 6: The tight-sibling lemma: the six-axis formation law keeps its memory for p >= 453. OPEN LEMMA of block 33 (PR #8177; setting in blocks 25, 30, 32: PRs #8168, #8174, #8176). Two-level noisy majority automaton in level time on Z^3: a site's three predecessors are z - e_1, z - e_2, z - e_3; seeds S (no 1-predecessor), amplified sites A (exactly one), processed sites (two or more). Counted family of marked explanation trees; rooted value v(z) := min over trees of the family containing z with all nodes at levels <= level(z) of E - 3(|S| - 1) - |A|; a site is TIGHT when v = 0. PROVED there: the extension lemma v(z) <= 1 + v(u) for a 1-predecessor u (amplified z: -1 + v(u)) and the seed lemma v(z) <= v(p) - 1 by a fork placed below the seed's level; the induction v <= 0 closes in every case but one. THE LEMMA: a processed site all of whose 1-predecessors are tight processed sites has a rooted tree of cost at most zero. It is equivalent to the unit budget c* = 1 and would lower the proved ordering threshold on the line (p,1,2) from 4165 to 453. Evidence: no violation in about 10^4 hill-climbed realizations; structural searches found no tight sibling pairs at all. Tools on this branch: probes/lib/family.py (automaton, kinds, trees, exact single-seed DP), probes/lib/rooted.py and mintree.py (integer programs for v and c*), probes/lib/violate.py, tightpairs.py, structural.py (searches). Routes nobody has tried: (i) prove that two tight processed siblings cannot share a processed successor (a local statement about marks in the 2x2x2 cone below z); (ii) a potential-function argument: find a weight on marks that v dominates; (iii) strengthen the induction hypothesis (carry the number of tight predecessors); (iv) a counterexample built by hand from the two-level period of block 31. title: Repair block 17's chessboard step and find the true constant
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Repair block 17's chessboard step and find the true constant. DEFECT found by a probe and confirmed (issue list: J:attack:PR8151): in block 17 (PR #8151, the static six-axis law's ordered side) T3 disseminates the event 'the canonical direction-i bond of the cell is bad' by reflections through site planes and states the result as 'every direction-i bond is bad'. Site reflections preserve the parity of the transverse coordinates, so the realized event is the direction-i bonds with even transverse coordinates (N/2 in 2D, N/4 in 3D), and T4's epsilon = 6m/p, hence T7's threshold p >= 216 max(q,r), does not follow. TASK: a correct chain with the best constant you can prove. Candidates: (i) a lemma that recovers the 2D statement (combine the four parity classes by a second chessboard or by Cauchy-Schwarz over classes); (ii) reflections through BOND planes (planes between sites): decide exactly for which weights (p, q, r) the six-axis law is reflection positive there, since those reflections move parity; (iii) cells of side two, so that one cell carries all parity classes; (iv) a Peierls count on the coarser lattice of even sites. COMPUTED LEAD for (ii): reflection positivity through a bond plane needs the 6 x 6 weight matrix W (p same axis, q opposite, r orthogonal) positive semidefinite; its eigenvalues are p+q+4r, p-q (three times), p+q-2r (twice), so the condition is p >= q and p + q >= 2r: on the line (p,1,2) that is p >= 3, the whole regime of interest; bond reflections move the parity that site reflections preserve. Verify this before relying on it. State the threshold you prove in 2D and in 3D and verify every finite inequality on small tori exactly (the probe's script is probes/work/pr8151/). title: The sphere formation law forgets its initial plane on the infinite lattice

SETTING (blocks 39 and 40, open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move' and 'ail40'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record; two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega the rule's pair weights), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; motion is pair-weight transit, in detailed balance with this law; formation happens at rate z * Z_x with content drawn from the rule.
